subject: science
notes: Sound travels as waves of alternating high and low air pressure.
When two sound waves meet so that the high-pressure parts of one line up with the low-pressure parts of the other, they cancel each other out, a process called destructive interference.
Noise-canceling headphones contain small microphones that detect incoming sound.
A circuit then generates a sound wave that is the mirror image of the incoming noise, with high pressure wherever the noise has low pressure.
Active noise cancellation works best on steady, low-pitched sounds such as engine hum.
stem: The student wants to explain to an audience unfamiliar with destructive interference how noise-canceling headphones reduce noise. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: When the high-pressure parts of one sound wave line up with the low-pressure parts of another, the two waves cancel each other out.
choices.B: Noise-canceling headphones reduce noise through destructive interference, producing a wave that is the mirror image of the incoming sound.
choices.C: Using small microphones to detect incoming sound, noise-canceling headphones work best on steady, low-pitched noises such as engine hum.
choices.D: Noise-canceling headphones detect incoming noise and emit a mirror-image wave whose high pressure meets the noise's low pressure, so the two cancel.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: explain how the headphones work, and do so for readers who do not know the term "destructive interference." The key must describe the mechanism in plain terms: the headphones create a wave whose high pressure meets the noise's low pressure, so the waves cancel.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This explains the physics in plain terms but never connects it to headphones.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This names the process and the mirror-image wave, but an audience unfamiliar with destructive interference would not understand why a mirror-image wave reduces noise. It is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This mentions the microphones and when the headphones work best, but it does not explain how they reduce noise.
explanation.D: Correct. It explains the whole process without relying on the technical term: detect the noise, produce a mirror-image wave, and let high and low pressure cancel.
